summary: The root "ljA" means to seek refuge or shelter. The eighth form, "iltajā," carries the same meaning, emphasizing the act of resorting to someone or something for protection.

headwords.def: لجّأ , inf. n. تَلْجِئَةٌ , He forced a person to do a thing against his will: (S, K:) or, to do a thing which was contrary to what it appeared to be. (AHeyth.) تَلْجِئَةٌ is also explained as signifying The leaving one's property to some one or more of his heirs, in preference to, or to the exclusion of, the other or others. لجّأ He so left his property. (ISh.) See 4.

headwords.def: الجأه إِلى شَىْءٍ He constrained, compelled, forced, drove, or necessitated, him to have recourse to, or to betake himself to, or to repair to, or to do, a thing; he impelled him, or drove him, against his will, to it, or to do it; (S, * Mgh, Msb, K, * TA;) as also إِلَيْهِ . (Mgh, Msb.) الجأ أَمْرَهُ إِلَى اللّٰهِ , (S, K,) and [ إِلَى اللّٰهِ ] , and , and (TA,) He referred, or committed, his affair to God. (S, K.) الجأه He protected him, defended him. (K.) Also said of a place, [ It protected him; afforded him refuge. ] (K, art. حرز .) الجأه إِلَى شَىْءٍ is also said when one has defended another, [as] in a place of refuge; [and app. may be rendered He caused him to have recourse to a thing, as to a place of refuge ]. (TA.)

headwords.def: لَجَأٌ and (S, K) and (K, art. لحد ; &c.) A place to which one has recourse for refuge, protection, preservation, concealment, covert, or lodging; a place of refuge; an asylum; a refuge. (S, K.) The hemzeh of the ↓ second is sometimes elided; and this is done to assimilate the word to مَنْجَا , when it is used therewith; like as منجا is written with hemzeh to assimilate it in the like case to مَلْجَأٌ . [ is often applied to a man: and you say also,] فُلَانٌ حَسَنُ [ Such a one is a good person to whom to have recourse for protection or concealment ]. The pl. of لَجَأٌ is أَلْجَآءٌ . (TA.) لَجَأٌ (assumed tropical:) A wife. (L.) An heir. (ISh.) [See 2.] The frog: (K:) or a kind of tortoise, that lives on the land and in the sea:
